_comment: Auth guards the public-route allowlist test recognises. A middleware that
is NOT listed here counts as NOT auth, so a route protected only by an
unlisted or anonymous wrapper shows up as public and fails
server/tests/public-route-allowlist.test.js. Adding a guard here is a
deliberate, reviewed change: it must fail closed (reject the request when
the credential is missing or invalid) and must not be a soft/optional check.
Fields: name = exported (or file-local) identifier; module = file that
defines it; local = defined in a route file rather than exported from
server/middleware; factory = called with arguments to produce the guard
deliberately lets through, with the path RELATIVE TO WHERE THE GUARD
EXECUTES (Express strips the mount prefix from req.path inside mounted
middleware); those routes must be in the allowlist.

guards.name: adminAuthenticate
guards.what: staff JWT (admin or technician row, token version, terminal scope rejected)

guards.name: requireAdmin
guards.what: 403 unless req.techRole === 'admin'; standalone it always 403s, so it fails closed

guards.name: requireTechOrAdmin
guards.what: 403 unless req.techRole is admin/technician; standalone it always 403s, so it fails closed

guards.name: authenticateAllowInactive
guards.what: customer JWT admitting inactive (not deleted) customers; routes must gate per-action

guards.name: validateTwilioSignature
guards.what: Twilio X-Twilio-Signature HMAC over the reconstructed public URL

guards.name: linkWorkerAuth
guards.what: Hermes worker HMAC-signed header (timestamp + nonce + body hash) or per-endpoint bearer

guards.name: mcpAuth
guards.what: GATE_MCP_READ_TOOLS + MCP_SERVICE_TOKEN bearer via constant-time compare

guards.name: terminalAuthenticate
guards.what: staff JWT that also admits terminal-scoped tokens minted by /validate-handoff (adminAuthenticate rejects that scope)

guards.name: adminAuthenticateExceptOauthCallback
guards.what: adminAuthenticate + requireAdmin for the whole Gmail router except Google's OAuth redirect target

_passthroughs_comment: Reviewed reject-or-next middleware that deliberately runs BEFORE an auth
guard in the same chain. A guard preceded by anything NOT in this list is
voided (an unknown handler could serve the response before the guard
runs), so keeping a guard countable behind a leading middleware requires
registering that middleware here. The bar for an entry: it either calls
next() or rejects the request outright — it must never serve data or

passthroughs.name: devOnly
passthroughs.what: 404 in production (hide dev-only routes from scanners) before the auth chain runs

passthroughs.name: devOnly
passthroughs.what: 404 in production before the auth chain runs

passthroughs.name: devOnly
passthroughs.what: 404 in production before the auth chain runs

passthroughs.name: devOnly
passthroughs.what: 404 in production before the auth chain runs

passthroughs.name: requireAiContentReport
passthroughs.what: 404 while the report surface is dark (unobservable-when-dark contract) before auth

passthroughs.name: chatReportLimiter
passthroughs.what: express-rate-limit instance ahead of authenticate — 429s or next(), never serves

passthroughs.name: rejectQueryString
passthroughs.what: 400 on any query string (recording-audio URL hygiene) before the auth chain

passthroughs.name: createBodyErrorHandler
passthroughs.what: factory for the JSON-RPC body-parser error handler — 413/parse-error JSON or next(err)

passthroughs.name: noStore
passthroughs.what: cache/robots/referrer header stamp for tokenized public surfaces — always next()

passthroughs.name: requireStaffTokenForLargeBody
passthroughs.what: 401 on a large body without a staff token, next() otherwise — never serves

passthroughs.name: publicMcpGate
passthroughs.what: 404 while GATE mcpPublic is off (unobservable-when-dark) ahead of parse/limits

passthroughs.name: publicA2aGate
passthroughs.what: 404 while GATE a2aPublic is off (unobservable-when-dark) ahead of parse/limits

passthroughs.name: commitmentsGate
passthroughs.what: 404 while GATE_HERMES_COMMITMENTS is off ahead of auth, limiter, and reads

passthroughs.name: watchdogGate
passthroughs.what: 404 while GATE_HERMES_WATCHDOG is off (unobservable-when-dark) ahead of linkWorkerAuth — no audit row while dark

passthroughs.name: staffMaintenance
passthroughs.what: 503 for staff HTTP requests during a maintenance window, next() otherwise — never serves

passthroughs.name: notFound
passthroughs.what: terminal 404 JSON for unmatched routes — never serves data

passthroughs.name: errorHandler
passthroughs.what: terminal error shaper (redacted log + status JSON) — never serves data
CORS headers; terminates only OPTIONS preflights with header-only responses
request logging — always next()
any express-rate-limit instance — 429s or next()s, never serves route data

passthroughs.name: json
passthroughs.what: body parser — 4xx on a malformed/oversized body, next() otherwise

passthroughs.name: urlencoded
passthroughs.what: body parser — 4xx on a malformed/oversized body, next() otherwise

passthroughs.name: raw
passthroughs.what: body parser — 4xx on an oversized body, next() otherwise

_routerConsumers_comment: Functions reviewed as safe to RECEIVE the app or a router as an argument
WITHOUT registering routes on it. Any other call that passes the app/a
router to an unanalysed function is a scanner problem — package code can
call app.get() just as well as in-repo code.

routerConsumers.name: createServer
routerConsumers.what: wraps the app as a request listener; registers no routes; must receive THE APP (the scanned root)

routerConsumers.name: setupExpressErrorHandler
routerConsumers.what: appends Sentry's error-capture middleware; registers no routes; must receive THE APP

routerConsumers.name: attachSockets
routerConsumers.what: Socket.IO server on the http handle — serves the /socket.io/ Engine.IO handshake (JWT-gated at connection); no Express routes

routerConsumers.name: attachVoiceRelay
routerConsumers.what: ElevenLabs voice-agent WebSocket relay on the http handle; upgrade-only listener, no Express routes
